issues.description: `delimiter` argument complects two concerns: parsing strategy selection and the literal split character
issues.detail: The `_PARAM_VALUE_DELIMITERS` map conflates 'symbolic style name' (pipeDelimited) with 'literal char to split on' (|). One concept, two domains, one argument. A caller passing `delimiter='|'` and `delimiter='pipeDelimited'` mean the same thing but read differently. Separate: accept either a 1-char string OR a named style constant, and document which is which. Right now this is EASY-NOT-SIMPLE.

issues.description: Runtime ValueError for unsupported delimiter is a place-oriented failure mode that the type system should catch
issues.detail: `delimiter: str | None` accepts any string, then validates at call time against a small allowlist. The set of valid delimiters is closed and known at definition. A `Literal[',', '|', ' ', 'pipeDelimited', 'spaceDelimited']` annotation moves the check from runtime-on-every-request to once-at-type-check. COMPLECTED: validation logic intertwined with split logic when it could be pushed to the edge (the signature).

issues.description: Silent no-op when `delimiter` is passed but param is already a list is a surprising time-dependent behavior
issues.detail: The behavior of `get_param_as_list('x', delimiter='|')` depends on whether the param arrived as one string or multiple instances — a fact about the HTTP request the caller often doesn't know. The docstring notes this, but the value/identity confusion is real: same call, different result based on upstream state. Consider whether silent skip is right or whether an explicit mode is simpler.

issues.description: The question that should have been asked: why is this a method argument instead of a request option?
issues.detail: `auto_parse_qs_csv` already exists as a RequestOptions flag governing query-string splitting. Adding `delimiter` as a per-call argument means every call site that wants pipe-delimited behavior must remember to pass it. A request-level (or route-level) parameter style declaration would be more aligned with how OpenAPI actually models this. Worth a hammock before shipping the per-call API.

review.summary: The feature is small and the implementation is a six-line split, which is good. But the `delimiter` argument is EASY-NOT-SIMPLE: it complects 'name of an OpenAPI style' with 'literal character to split on' in one untyped string, then validates at runtime what the type system could check at definition time. The deeper question — whether per-call delimiter is the right shape at all, given that `auto_parse_qs_csv` already exists as a request option and OpenAPI styles are per-parameter declarations — appears not to have been asked. Ship it if you must, but a `Literal[...]` annotation costs nothing and removes the runtime ValueError path entirely.
